title: Nvidia is turning its massive cash pile into its next competitive moat
excerpt: Nvidia is turning its massive cash pile into a competitive moat, and now it's bringing Wall Street capital into its AI ecosystem.
content_html:
Nvidia's next moat is something chip rivals can't copy: its giant pile of money

By Geoff Weiss

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Majestic Labs cofounder Sha Rabii knows what it's like to build AI infrastructure in an industry dominated by Nvidia.

Rabii spent years leading custom silicon inside Google and Meta before launching his own AI hardware startup.

When Rabii considers Nvidia's biggest competitive advantage, he doesn't point to its brilliant engineers, leading technology, or well-established sales channels.

"Where they're kind of unmatched is in the giant bag of cash they're sitting on top of," Rabii said.

Nvidia had more than $80 billion in cash and marketable investments as of April, when it last reported earnings, and generated another $50 billion in operating cash flow that quarter. While other Big Tech giants have comparable stashes, Nvidia doesn't shoulder the same massive data-center construction costs.

Even after returning billions to shareholders, it leaves it with an enviable problem: how to put its riches to work.

"What better use of the rest of the cash to invest and grow and strengthen the ecosystem around their products?" said Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon.

On Monday, Nvidia unveiled a new way to turbo-charge the power of its cash hoard by bringing in at least $500 billion of outside capital to finance far more Nvidia-powered AI infrastructure than what it's already funding. This new initiative includes some of the biggest firms on Wall Street, including Apollo, Blackstone, and Goldman Sachs.

The company is also in talks to guarantee an OpenAI data center project worth hundreds of billions of dollars. It's providing financial backstops to neoclouds, or specialized AI cloud providers, to buy its graphics processing units (GPUs) — the chips used to run AI.

It's also making long-term commitments to secure scarce components, and investing in and supporting AI startups through its NVentures and Inception programs. If one bet takes off, Nvidia hits the lottery on both the investment and future chip sales.

The result is a self-reinforcing cycle: Nvidia's technological dominance generates cash, and that cash is increasingly becoming a moat of its own.

Nvidia's scale has boosted its financing playbook

Vendors using their balance sheets to help customers buy their products isn't a novel strategy, said Bernie Margulies, who works on GPU financing at American Compute. The practice is spreading more broadly.

AMD has previously backstopped chips for customers, while Broadcom recently partnered with Apollo and Blackstone on an AI-infrastructure financing platform. Neither rival can match Nvidia's scale, said D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria, calling the chipmaker's financial might a different "order of magnitude."

In addition, Meta agreed to purchase up to $15 billion of computing capacity from the neocloud Nebius, while Google has backed Anthropic's data-center projects.

Historically, Nvidia hasn't needed to do this, Margulies said.

As the AI buildout explodes, Nvidia helps finance projects that might not otherwise get built. Margulies said this could also be read as an effort to keep customers from experimenting with alternatives, like AI chips built by AMD or Google.

Alex Yeh, CEO of the neocloud GMI Cloud — which has a backstop agreement with Nvidia — said the deals help the chip giant build an "alliance" with neoclouds and AI startups as its biggest cloud customers develop their own chips.

They can also unlock massive orders for AI chips.

Yeh said that without Nvidia stepping in, he wouldn't have been able to take on the AI startup Fireworks as a customer, with which GMI has a nine-figure deal.

Likewise, Rabii said financing is a complication for one of Majestic's target markets: neoclouds. If a customer wanted to buy billions of dollars of Majestic hardware, his startup couldn't backstop the financing the way Nvidia can.

"Nvidia's real moat today is how freaking expensive it is to build data centers," Rabii said. Instead, he said he's betting Majestic's power-efficient chips will convince customers to choose its systems.

Nvidia is looking beyond its own balance sheet

Nvidia's growing financial ties have fueled concerns about circular financing.

Margulies said he isn't particularly concerned, though the strategy "does cause a lot of investors to be worried." If Nvidia loses market share and has to pay out on its backstops, "it'll be brutal," he said.

Michael Reid, CEO of Australian neocloud Megaport, which does not have a backstop agreement with Nvidia, said overall demand for GPUs provides another safeguard. If one customer falters, the neocloud could rent the capacity to another.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said on X that the company's latest Wall Street partnerships are designed to address concerns about circular financing. Analysts said that tapping outside capital means Nvidia doesn't have to shoulder as much of the financial risk.

"They're sharing the reward, but they're also sharing the risk," said D.A. Davidson's Luria.

In this vein, the chipmaker's next financial moat may be access to money that isn't even its own.

英伟达的下一条护城河是芯片竞争对手无法复制的：巨额资金

作者：Geoff Weiss 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

Majestic Labs 联合创始人 Sha Rabii 知道在 Nvidia 主导的行业中构建人工智能基础设施是什么样的。

在推出自己的人工智能硬件初创公司之前，拉比花了数年时间在谷歌和 Meta 内部领导定制芯片。

当拉比考虑英伟达最大的竞争优势时，他并没有指出英伟达卓越的工程师、领先的技术或完善的销售渠道。

拉比说：“他们无与伦比的地方在于他们手握的巨额现金。”

截至 4 月份（上次公布收益时），英伟达拥有超过 800 亿美元的现金和可流通投资，并在该季度另外产生了 500 亿美元的运营现金流。 虽然其他大型科技巨头也有类似的储备，但英伟达并没有承担同样巨大的数据中心建设成本。

即使在向股东返还数十亿美元之后，它仍然面临着一个令人羡慕的问题：如何利用其财富。

“还有什么更好的方法来利用剩余的现金来投资、发展和加强围绕其产品的生态系统呢？” 伯恩斯坦分析师史黛西·拉斯贡说。

周一，英伟达推出了一种新方法，通过引入至少 5000 亿美元的外部资本来增强其现金储备的力量，为英伟达支持的人工智能基础设施提供比其已经资助的资金更多的资金。 这项新计划的参与者包括华尔街一些最大的公司，包括阿波罗、黑石和高盛。

该公司还正在就价值数千亿美元的 OpenAI 数据中心项目进行担保谈判。 它为 Neoclouds 或专门的人工智能云提供商提供财务支持，以购买其图形处理单元（GPU）——用于运行人工智能的芯片。

它还做出长期承诺，确保稀缺组件的安全，并通过其 NVentures 和 Inception 计划投资和支持人工智能初创企业。 如果赌注成功，英伟达就在投资和未来芯片销售方面都中了彩票。

结果是一个自我强化的循环：英伟达的技术主导地位产生了现金，而这些现金正日益成为自己的护城河。

英伟达的规模提升了其融资策略

美国计算公司 (American Compute) 从事 GPU 融资工作的伯尼·马古利斯 (Bernie Margulies) 表示，供应商利用其资产负债表来帮助客户购买其产品并不是什么新颖的策略。 这种做法正在更广泛地传播。

AMD 此前曾为客户提供芯片支持，而博通最近与 Apollo 和 Blackstone 合作开发了人工智能基础设施融资平台。 D.A. 表示，这两个竞争对手都无法与 Nvidia 的规模相媲美。 戴维森分析师吉尔·卢里亚（Gil Luria）称，这家芯片制造商的财务状况可能是一个不同的“数量级”。

此外，Meta 同意从 Neocloud Nebius 购买高达 150 亿美元的计算能力，而谷歌则支持 Anthropic 的数据中心项目。

马古利斯说，从历史上看，英伟达不需要这样做。

随着人工智能建设的爆炸式增长，英伟达为原本可能无法建设的项目提供融资。 马古利斯表示，这也可以被解读为阻止客户尝试替代方案的努力，例如 AMD 或谷歌制造的人工智能芯片。

neocloud GMI Cloud 的首席执行官 Alex Yeh 表示，这些交易有助于这家芯片巨头与 neoclouds 和人工智能初创公司建立“联盟”，因为其最大的云客户开发自己的芯片。该公司与 Nvidia 签署了支持协议。

他们还可以解锁人工智能芯片的大量订单。

Yeh 表示，如果没有 Nvidia 的介入，他就无法将人工智能初创公司 Fireworks 作为客户，GMI 与该公司签订了九位数的协议。

同样，Rabii 表示，对于 Majestic 的目标市场之一：neoclouds 来说，融资是一个复杂的问题。 如果客户想要购买数十亿美元的 Majestic 硬件，他的初创公司无法像 Nvidia 那样提供融资支持。

“今天英伟达真正的护城河是建造数据中心的成本惊人，”拉比说。 相反，他表示他相信 Majestic 的节能芯片将说服客户选择其系统。

英伟达正在超越自身的资产负债表

英伟达日益增长的金融关系引发了人们对循环融资的担忧。

马古利斯表示，他并不特别担心，尽管该策略“确实引起了很多投资者的担忧”。 如果英伟达失去市场份额并必须支付其支持费用，“这将是残酷的，”他说。

澳大利亚 neocloud Megaport 的首席执行官 Michael Reid 表示，GPU 的总体需求提供了另一个保障。该公司没有与 Nvidia 签订支持协议。 如果一个客户出现问题，neocloud 可以将容量租给另一个客户。

英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在 X 上表示，该公司最新的华尔街合作伙伴关系旨在解决对循环融资的担忧。 分析师表示，利用外部资本意味着英伟达不必承担那么多的财务风险。

“他们在分享回报，但他们也在分担风险，”D.A. 戴维森的卢里亚。

在这种情况下，这家芯片制造商的下一个金融护城河可能是获得甚至不属于自己的资金。
